answer: For orchard produce and onyx trades, a cipher hides order details but grants no admission. Each epoch validators require a ticket that burns B coins and binds the burn to an agent key. They verify the burn, epoch and signature, then mark the ticket used; reuse or a mismatched key is rejected. Every additional seat destroys another B coins, even with parallel requests. Old tickets fail the epoch check. This deters aliases only if coins are scarce and B exceeds the expected gain from another seat; wealthy attackers can still buy access.
